intro: The Oracle is not merely a program; it is a digital reflection of the ancient Akashic records. Every month corresponds to a specific celestial vibration that shapes the mythological creature you resonate with. What follows is the surviving lore, gathered chapter by chapter, of how the Oracle came to speak.

articles.title: The Founding Myth
body: Before the twelve orders were named, there was only the Wheel — a single band of light circling a dark that had not yet learned to hold stars. The first Oracle was not a person or a machine but a question, asked by the Wheel itself: what does each turning make of the ones born beneath it?

The answer took the form of twelve creatures, each drawn from a different arc of the turning sky, each carrying a piece of the Wheel's own nature forward into the world. They did not choose their months. The months chose them, the way a shoreline chooses its tide.

articles.title: The Spirit Guides
body: Every soul is assigned a guide — a manifestation of their higher consciousness — to navigate the trials of the physical plane. The guide is not a separate being so much as a mirror held at the correct angle, showing back the quality a soul most needs and most resists.
Guides do not command. They accompany. The Silver Owl does not tell the Storm Griffin where to fly; it simply flies alongside, so the Griffin remembers it was never truly circling alone.

articles.title: The Legendary Artifacts
body: The artifacts named in each reading are not physical items, but energetic imprints that represent your innate talents and spiritual tools — the Chalice of Ages, the Bow of Distant Horizons, the Vial of Rebirth. To 'hold' one is a figure of speech for a capacity you already carry.

Some Oracle-keepers argue the artifacts are older than the creatures themselves — that the twelve beasts were shaped around tools that already existed, the way a hand grows to fit the shape of the thing it has always been meant to carry.

articles.title: Celestial Alignment
body: The position of the planets at the moment of your birth month creates a unique harmonic resonance, known as your Alignment. Unlike a natal chart, which fixes a single instant, an Alignment is closer to a key signature — the underlying tone every note of your life is played against.
An Alignment can be strained by circumstance without ever truly breaking. Oracle-keepers describe this as 'the bent note that still belongs to the song.'

articles.title: Cusps and Blended Fates
body: Those born within three days of a month's start or end may possess secondary traits of the adjacent month's creature — a kind of dual citizenship in the celestial order. A Phoenix born on the cusp of the Whispering Sphinx, for instance, may carry the Sphinx's discernment beneath its usual radiance.

Cusp-born souls are not asked to choose one creature over the other. The Oracle regards them as living proof that the Wheel's twelve divisions were always somewhat approximate — useful lines drawn across something that was, underneath, continuous.

articles.title: The Four Realms and the Wheel
body: The twelve creatures are further grouped into four realms — Ignis, Terra, Aether, and Abyss — each governed by one of the four classical elements. A creature's realm describes its temperament in broad strokes, the weather it is most at home in, even when its month gives it a more particular shape.

No realm is considered superior to another. Oracle-keepers are fond of reminding visitors that fire needs earth to have something to burn, air needs fire to have something to carry, water needs air to become weather, and earth needs water to become anything at all.

articles.title: How Readings Are Divined
body: A reading begins the moment a birth month is spoken or written, whether aloud in the old rite or typed into the Oracle's modern gate. The Oracle does not calculate a fate; it recognizes one already present, the way a key does not create a lock but simply confirms it fits.

Accuracy, the Oracle-keepers insist, depends less on the mechanism than on the willingness of the one asking to look inward honestly. A reading is a mirror, not a verdict — what you do with what it shows you remains entirely your own.
